source.title: Interpreting Large Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Dictionary Learning
source.authors: Stepan Shabalin; Ayush Panda; Dmitrii Kharlapenko; A. Ali; Yixiong Hao; Arthur Conmy

record.tranche_reason: The study compares automated interpretability scores for SAE features, ITDA features, and MLP neurons in a text-to-image diffusion model. This is a different measurement and setting from the original neuron audit.
record.gate_note: The study reports autointerpretability scores relevant to tool-based interpretability comparisons. It does not report a share of units with one or two jobs, independent audits of language models, attribution graphs, or a test of explanation predictions on explicitly held-out activations. Reconstruction and steering results do not directly test the listed versions. Prior results about language-model neuron explanations are cited background, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs and ITDA on FLUX.1 Schnell, a text-to-image diffusion transformer, and uses MLP neurons only as a baseline in a visual autointerp comparison. No version is tested. V1, V2 and V7 concern language-model neurons, and V7 specifically concerns simulation scoring on new text. V4 concerns the share of interpretable neurons rising with better neuron-interpretation tools or architectures. Showing that SAE features score higher than neurons compares a different unit; it does not measure a neuron share under better tools. V6 is not tested because scoring uses max-activating examples, not held-out activations. The neuron-versus-SAE result bears on the broad claim but fits no stated version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that SAEs and ITDA decompose FLUX.1 residual activations into interpretable, steerable features and beat MLP neurons on autointerp. They add that autointerp misses qualitative SAE/ITDA differences: ITDA features capture attributes, while SAE features capture objects.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a visual explainer and image classifier to describe and score activation patterns in a text-to-image diffusion model, rather than language-model explanations of neuron activations. It compares SAE and ITDA features with MLP neurons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported interpretability comparison is for layer 18 and k=64, dictionary size 64000; other layers and configurations are not the conditions of the autointerpretability scores in Figure 7.

fits_no_version.finding: In FLUX.1 Schnell layer 18, MLP neurons get lower visual autointerp scores (mean 0.654) than SAE (0.819) and ITDA (0.776) features. A few neurons score very highly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a large diffusion transformer, individual MLP neurons are less interpretable by automated visual scoring than dictionary-learned features of the same layer.

record.problems: The interpretability evaluation is an automated visual scoring pipeline using the same Gemini backend for explanation and scoring. The paper notes possible bias toward simple image characteristics such as color and leaves detailed investigation for future work. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the scores.
record.rows_left_out: No other results meeting the row criteria were omitted.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit shares are not tested.
No language models or MoE models are tested, and there is no scale comparison.
There is no InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
There is no comparison of neuron interpretability across tools, architectures or regularization, and no share of interpretable neurons.
There are no attribution graphs or circuits.
Explanations are scored on max-activating examples, not held-out activations.
There is no simulation scoring of language-model neurons on new text, and no variation of the explainer model.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. Better dictionary methods beating neurons is, if anything, the superposition view, and it is not evidence that neuron interpretability rises with better tools. The explainer and scorer share one Gemini backend. No uncertainty is reported, and the authors flag a possible color bias.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit and its reported percentages are not tested.
No other language models, dense or mixture-of-experts language-model comparison, or scaling to trillions of parameters is tested.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron or recursive-generalization account is tested.

The study compares interpretability scores for SAE and ITDA features with MLP neurons, but does not measure a share of interpretable neurons or test the proposed causes of messy neurons, compare architectures, or report InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.
No attribution graphs or reconstruction of model behaviour using the model's own neurons are tested.
The paper does not state that explanations are tested on activations or examples independent of those used to form the explanations.
The study scores visual feature explanations in a diffusion model, not neuron explanations on new text; it does not test whether a minority of neurons score well with stronger explainer models.

rows.subject: FLUX.1 Schnell
rows.operation_detail: Automated visual interpretability scoring of activating MLP neuron patterns
rows.note: The paper says MLP neurons are generally less interpretable than SAE and ITDA features, while some MLP neurons have exceedingly high scores.
rows.check: This is a diffusion-model MLP-neuron autointerp score, not a language model, so V4 is not tested. It is a single tool with no baseline for a share of interpretable neurons. Scoring uses a Gemini image judge on max-activating examples. The mean and median of 0.654/0.650 are read from Figure 7.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Figure 7 (lines 503-504; MLP panel by elimination, since SAE and ITDA panels are labelled); setup Section 5.2 lines 446-453

relation.reason: The study discusses neuron interpretability only as a baseline to compare against its dictionary-learning methods. It does not test any version.

tranche.reason: The study applies SAEs and ITDA to FLUX.1 Schnell, a text-to-image diffusion transformer. MLP neurons are only an autointerp baseline for its own methods. It reports no share of interpretable neurons and no comparison of tools or architectures for neurons, so no version is tested.

source_check.notes: Values appear only in the Figure 7 histogram text, where the panel titles are garbled. The 0.654/0.650 pair is the MLP panel by elimination. Autointerp is image-level detection: Gemini 2.0 Flash explains and scores (0-1), at layer 18 with k=64 and d=64000. It does not simulate activations on text, so V7 does not apply. The Appendix D prompts are the study's own pipeline prompts, not instructions to a reader.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: FLUX.1 Schnell, layer 18, automated visual scoring
reader_labels.reason: SAE and ITDA feature scores exceed the MLP-neuron scores in the reported means and medians (r1–r3), consistent with better tools yielding more interpretable features in this tested setting.
